messages:
jess: :rotating_light: FYI rolling canary for inference-service v2.3.1 started 2m ago. telemetry shows increasing 504s on canary nodes after node-drain. grabbing logs now.
sam: seeing crashloops on the canary pods, 3/5 in CrashLoopBackOff. perf dashboards spike on latency and pod restarts. paging oncall.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident created (PD-98765) and paged to sam (oncall). Severity P1.
pagerduty: page sent to @sam - acknowledge to start mitigation.
sam: acked. I'm taking triage. can anyone check recent manifest changes? did we change HPA or probing on this rollout?
leo: looking at the canary manifest from the release job. quick dump:```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-hpa-canary
spec:
  minReplicas: 0
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 60
```
leo: uh oh minReplicas=0 for canary — if nodes are drained we can end up with zero desirable pods and the autoscaler may not scale up quickly. also readiness probe looks strict in this deploy (long startup checks).
maria: logs from one pod:```
Container start failed: failed to create containerd task: OCI runtime create failed: container_linux.go:344: starting container process caused "exec: \"/app/start\": stat /app/start: no such file or directory"
```
maria: that suggests image/tarball path mismatch in this build or the start binary missing in the image. combined with minReplicas=0 that's brutal.
ops-tilly: can we toggle the feature flag to stop traffic to the canary? ff key inference_v2_canary -> set false now.
leo: flipping the FF via LaunchDarkly API now: `curl -X PATCH https://ld.api/... -d '{"key":"inference_v2_canary","on":false}'` — done. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: automatic rollback policy triggered for inference-service (canary failures). Initiating rollback to v2.3.0 as configured.
sam: I'm going to patch the HPA to minReplicas:1 to avoid zero-desire while we investigate the image. applying patch: `kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa-canary -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":1}]'`
jess: doing a quick restart of the remaining canary pods after the patch: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-canary -n prod`
maria: after restart and HPA patch pods are scheduling but some still hit the start not found error — it looks like this build omitted the start binary (artifact pipeline bug). rollback should remove the bad pods from rotation.
sam: rollback completed and verified: traffic back to baseline, 5xx rate down to normal. stability check for 10m in progress.
leo: customer impact: estimated ~3% of requests across the cluster experienced 5xx for ~12 minutes during the canary window. flagged customers: enterprise-account-42 saw errors, support notified.
jess: opened incident triage doc and added timeline: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/IN-2026-canary-crashloop (pinned). schedule postmortem for tomorrow 10:30 PT.
incident-bot: Incident PD-98765 marked as mitigated by sam at 1912345850.
sam: handing off to leo for root cause and postmortem writeup. I'm on-call for another 25m if needed.
leo: will take ownership. initial action items: 1) revert artifact pipeline change that stripped binary, 2) add CI smoke to validate start binary presence, 3) change canary HPA template to minReplicas:1, 4) add deploy guard to prevent feature-flag+zero-min combo.
maria: recording commands and logs in the incident doc, will attach CLI traces and `kubectl describe` outputs.
jess: big thanks to everyone for quick rollback and flag kill-switch. :heart: please add any additional impact notes here and tag customers we should follow up with.
ops-tilly: marking this thread with postmortem required and setting priority to P1 for followup actions. :thumbsup:
leo: note for postmortem: investigate why the rollout job allowed a canary manifest with minReplicas:0 — probably templating bug in helm chart values for canaries.
sam: closing pagerduty for now, will reopen if regressions.
incident-bot: thread closed (mitigation complete).
